text:
Lina: quick follow-up from today's microbatching sync — noticed a race where synchronous prefetches for microbatched tiny pages conflict with immediate eviction, causing redundant NVMe writes and tail blips.

Ben: saw it on canary. flow: request finishes -> prefetch sync triggered for next-step tokens -> eviction completes and compacts same pages -> prefetch writes stale content.

Omar: two options: (1) move small-page prefetch to async bounded worker with cancel token, or (2) add lightweight generation tags so demote increments gen and prefetch abandons if gen changed before IO submit.

Lina: gen tags are low-cost and cancel early; combined with async worker they might be best. cancel semantics: only cancel before submission to NVMe. once queued, let it complete.

Ben: agree. also add a microbatch-aware prefetch heuristic: if batch_size <= 8, prefer async cap=4, if >8 allow sync up to 16 pages. keeps fast path for larger batches.

Omar: config sketch:
```
prefetch:
  microbatch:
    sync_threshold: 8
    sync_max_pages: 16
    async_inflight_cap: 4
  gen_cancel_ms: 5
```

Lina: observability: prefetch_cancel_before_io, prefetch_async_inflight, microbatch_prefetch_sync_hits, nvme_write_waste_bytes. tag by pool and tenant.

Ben: perf note: async worker must be admission-controlled to avoid nvme queue overload — use per-pool inflight counter + tenant weight. Also prefer coalesced IO for small pages (buffer up to 4ms or 32 pages).

Omar: for safety, when mem_pressure > 90% bypass async and force sync flushes. prefer correctness.

Lina: canary plan: flag behind feature toggle, roll to one hybrid pool, synthetic tests: microchat burst and long-form gen. Success: p99 tail down >=10% for microchat, no regression on long-form. Rollback if nvme qd rises >15% or any tenant p99 >2x.

sre-bot: canary created: microbatch-prefetch-gencanary-2026-06-10 02:00 UTC — auto-rollback hooks configured.

Ben: I'll draft RFC follow-up and PR with defaults. Omar: can you add metrics and the inflight gating?

Omar: on it. I'll also add a small synthetic reproducer for microbatch races.

Lina: thanks — end here.
